correctness.rationale: A complete 18-edge graph model matches LCF [5,-5]^6; exhaustive branching over unmatched graph vertices enumerates 17 perfect matchings. The 761 nonempty faces support 377 disjoint codimension-one matching pairs and seven precisely specified critical cells. All 2610 face incidences were oriented and topologically sorted, proving acyclicity (761 visited). Forman discrete Morse theory gives one 0-cell plus six 2-cells and hence a wedge of six 2-spheres. Independent full matching enumeration gives 72 nonextendible triples, no smaller obstructions. The packaged standard-library checker executes with VERIFY_OK; the claim is finite, not extrapolated.

evidence: Bayer–Jelic Milutinovic–Vega arXiv:2209.02803 proves cases for planar honeycomb H(1,m,n) and H(2,2,2), not a nonplanar 12-vertex cubic Franklin graph.
Chandrakar–Singh arXiv:2407.05809 theorem 1.1 covers 2-by-n grids and polygonal line tilings; the Franklin graph is nonplanar, so cannot be one of the planar graph inputs.
Agarwal–Basak arXiv:2608.30601 classifies two ladder families; for 12 vertices the circular ladder has 20 perfect matchings and the Mobius ladder 18, whereas the Franklin graph has 17.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest nearby family theorems have input restrictions failed by this graph. For the ladder families, differing exhaustive perfect-matching counts rule out graph isomorphism at equal order. A general fact that some perfect-matching complexes are wedges of spheres does not imply the exact number six in dimension two.

value.rationale: The Franklin graph is a historically central nonplanar, bipartite cubic graph associated with the Klein bottle. Its extendible-edge-subset complex is a canonical simplicial invariant; no known exact homotopy type followed from the existing ordinary matching-complex result. The calculation detects a sharp boundary at size-three matchings (72 missing triangles) while the one-skeleton is unchanged, and yields a six-dimensional integral H_2 rather than the ambient twelve-dimensional H_3. This supplies a motivated complete finite topological classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
